title: The Prosocial Ranking Challenge: Reducing Polarization on Social Media without Sacrificing Engagement
content: We report the first direct comparisons of multiple alternative social media algorithms on multiple platforms on outcomes of societal interest. We used a browser extension to modify which posts were shown to desktop social media users, randomly assigning 9,386 users to a control group or one of five alternative ranking algorithms which simultaneously altered content across three platforms for six months during the US 2024 presidential election. This reduced our preregistered index of affective polarization by an average of 0.03 standard deviations (p < 0.05), including a 1.5 degree decrease in differences between the 100 point inparty and outparty feeling thermometers. We saw reductions in active use time for Facebook (-0.37 min/day) and Reddit (-0.2 min/day), but an increase of 0.32 min/day (p < 0.01) for X/Twitter. We saw an increase in reports of negative social media experiences but found no effects on well-being, news knowledge, outgroup empathy, perceptions of and support for partisan violence. This implies that bridging content can improve some societal outcomes without necessarily conflicting with the engagement-driven business model of social media.

title: Adrian får ofte folk til å snu seg: – Jeg kvier meg alltid for å gå ut
content:
– Hadde jeg ikke hatt tourettes hadde jeg nok ikke hatt mye å prate om, sier 36-åringen og ler.
Adrian Lund skulle ofte ønske at han kunne gå opp Karl Johan og være anonym – bare gli inn blant menneskene uten at noen la merke til han.
Men slik er det ikke.
Adrian blir ofte lagt merke til, og det er noe han må leve med resten av livet.
– Jeg kvier meg alltid for å gå ut, men jeg må jo bare gjøre det, sier han.
Synlige tics
De ufrivillige klikkelydene med munnen, rykningene og bevegelsene i ansiktet og skuldrene er en del av hverdagen hans.
Noen ganger kan han også plutselig rekke fingeren mot andre uten å ville det.
– Det hadde sikkert på mange måter vært enklere å leve et liv uten tourettes. Samtidig tror jeg ikke at jeg hadde vært like lykkelig som jeg er i dag siden jeg har kommet meg styrket ut av det, forteller han.
Opptatt av åpenhet
I ti år har Adrian holdt foredrag om arbeidsmiljø, inkludering og mangfold, og om hvordan et ungdomsliv preget av tourettes, adhd, mobbing og utenforskap har satt sine spor.
I 2016 deltok han i «71 grader nord». Han har også vært med i flere podkaster og nylig vært med i NRKs TV-serie «Tabu», der han forteller om livet med tourettes.
Nå har han vunnet årets tabupris for sin åpenhet.
– Det er en veldig fin anerkjennelse for jobben jeg har gjort. Mye av det har vært for min egen del, men at folk har sett at det ikke er så skummelt å være åpen, det er veldig fint å se, sier Adrian.
Behov for mer kunnskap
Tove Gundersen, generalsekretær i Rådet for psykisk helse, forteller at det er første gang at en person med tourettes vinner tabuprisen.
– Adrian er en fantastisk person som bidrar til et mer inkluderende samfunn og viser frem en diagnose det ikke går an å skjule.
Gundersen mener at Tourettes syndrom har fått for lite plass i samfunnet.
– Adrian viser at det er mulig å snu frykt og ubehag til noe positivt. Vi trenger flere forbilder andre kan relatere seg til, og som bidrar til økt kunnskap om en tilstand folk kan leve godt med, sier hun.
Går aldri på kino
Adrian Lund vokste opp i Melbu i Nordland, men bor i dag i Buvika – et tettsted like utenfor Trondheim.
Da han var sju år gammel fikk han sine første ufrivillige tics. Som elleveåring fikk han diagnosen.
Selv om han har valgt å være åpen om livet med tourettes, er frykten og bekymringen for hvordan andre vil reagere, fortsatt til stede.
– Det er helt enkle ting som mange tar for gitt, men som jeg lar være å oppsøke. Jeg går for eksempel ikke på kino eller teater. Begravelser er også vanskelig, forklarer han.
Har blitt ufrivillig filmet av andre
Hans største redsel er at folk skal undervurdere han og kun se på han som en person med funksjonsnedsettelse.
– Det er noe med det å få folk til å se forbi førsteinntrykket – å se mennesket bak ticsene.
På grunn av mobbing i oppveksten, er ungdomsgjenger spesielt triggende for Adrian. Men noen av det verste opplevelsene har kommet fra godt voksne.
– Jeg har av og til opplevd at folk har filmet meg, men en episode jeg husker veldig godt fra i fjor, er en mann i 50-årene som satt to rader foran meg på flyet og startet å herme etter ticsene mine. Slike ting setter spor.
36-åringen er glad for at han kan være et ansikt utad og bidra til økt kunnskap om Tourettes syndrom.
– Tør å sette ord på det
– Hvilke råd vil du gi til barn og unge som vokser opp med tourettes?
– Tør å sette ord på det, og ei det. Det er ikke like morsomt å mobbe noen som adresserer det «rare» selv.
Han tror det ofte er frykten for andres reaksjoner som gjør det vanskelig å være åpen.
– Man undertrykker kanskje ticsene. Det er ofte skumlest før man har fått sagt det høyt, uavhengig av om man er ung eller voksen. Alt som har fått en forklaring, blir mindre skummelt. Da blir det også lettere for andre å spørre.

title: In Tajikistan, a system will be launched to identify dangerous mountain lakes
content:
Tajikistan has begun implementing the automated THAW (Transient Hydrologic Anomalies Weekly) tool to identify new and anomalously changing mountain lakes that may pose a danger due to the risk of outburst.
A practical workshop on the use of the tool took place on August 21 in Dushanbe at the Hydrometeorological Agency of the Committee for Environmental Protection under the Government of Tajikistan. Specialists from the Hydrometeorological Agency, the State Institution “Institute for the Study of Glaciers and the Cryosphere” of the National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan, as well as the Institute of Water Problems, Hydropower and Ecology of the National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan participated in it.
How THAW Works
THAW is an automated tool for monitoring surface water bodies that uses satellite radar observation data from Sentinel-1 SAR and the Google Earth Engine platform.
The tool makes it possible to regularly analyze changes in water bodies and identify potentially new or anomalously changing mountain lakes. Such changes can serve as a signal to specialists about the need for additional study and monitoring of a specific water body.
The use of satellite data is especially important for mountainous areas, where regular ground monitoring of many lakes is difficult due to complex terrain and the remoteness of certain territories.
Specialists Tested the System
In the practical part of the workshop, participants worked in groups and studied the capabilities of THAW to identify potentially emerging lakes in individual glacial basins of Central Asia.
Specialists also discussed methods for verifying the results obtained using the tool and the criteria by which the need for further monitoring of the identified water body is determined.
Special attention was paid to the exchange of experience between specialists and the identification of needs for further development of monitoring systems for mountain lakes and early warning systems for possible glacial lake outbursts.
Such systems are of particular importance for Tajikistan, a significant portion of whose territory is located in mountainous areas. Climate change and glacier melting can contribute to changes in the size and condition of mountain lakes, increasing the need for their regular observation.
Within the Framework of the GLOFCA Project
The workshop was held as part of the regional GLOFCA project — “Reducing the Vulnerability of the Population in the Central Asian Region to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods in the Context of Climate Change.”
The event was organized by the Hydrometeorological Agency of the Committee for Environmental Protection under the Government of Tajikistan in cooperation with the UNESCO Regional Office in Almaty and the University of Zurich.
The GLOFCA project is implemented by UNESCO with funding from the Adaptation Fund and is aimed at increasing the resilience of the Central Asian population to risks associated with glacial lake outbursts.
The implementation of modern remote monitoring tools, such as THAW, should help specialists detect changes in mountain water bodies more quickly, verify potentially dangerous objects, and improve observation and early warning systems.
The results and recommendations obtained during the workshop are planned to be used for further improvement of the tools, protocols, and monitoring systems applied within the framework of the GLOFCA project.

title: Reportaron la excarcelación de cinco militares presos políticos recluidos en Ramo Verde
content:
La Coalición por los Derechos Humanos y la Democracia informó este martes 18 de agosto la excarcelación de cinco militares presos políticos que permanecían recluidos en el Centro de Procesados Militares de Ramo Verde, en el estado Miranda.
De acuerdo con el reporte de la ONG, los excarcelados son el mayor César Alejandro Girón Contreras, el sargento mayor de tercera (SM3) Johandri Alberto Aguilar Leal, el sargento primero (S/1.º) Jhorman Enrique Jiménez, el sargento segundo (S/2.º) Jhonson Enrique García y el sargento segundo (S/2.º) Edwin José Noguera.
#Atencion Excarcelan a 5 militares presos políticos, quienes se encontraban recluidos en Ramo Verde, hoy 18 de agosto 2026.
— Coalición por los Derechos Humanos y la Democracia (@Coalicion_ddhh) August 18, 2026
Ellos son:
1._ Mayor César Girón
2._ SM3 Johandri Aguilar
3._ S1. Jhorman Jiménez
4._ S2. Jhonson García
5._ S2. Edwin Noguera
Los cinco militares salieron del centro de reclusión bajo medidas cautelares sustitutivas de la privación de libertad, por lo que la excarcelación no implica el cierre de los procesos judiciales que enfrentan.
Entre las condiciones impuestas se encuentra la presentación periódica ante los tribunales, la prohibición de salir de Venezuela y la restricción de ofrecer declaraciones públicas a medios de comunicación.
Estas excarcelaciones se producen en un contexto de liberaciones anunciadas por el gobierno encargado el pasado viernes, como parte del proceso de negociación que llevan el oficialismo y la oposición.
81 excarcelaciones confirmadas
Hasta el lunes 17 de agosto, la organización Foro Penal confirmó 81 excarcelaciones de presos políticos en Venezuela, de las 131 anunciadas por el gobierno encargado el 14 de agosto.
“Continúa el proceso de verificación de excarcelaciones iniciado el 14/08/26. Hasta este momento en el Foro Penal hemos verificado y confirmado 81 excarcelaciones. Seguimos…”, escribió Himiob en su cuenta de X.
Entre las personas cuya excarcelación fue confirmada por el Foro Penal se encuentran casos emblemáticos como Emirlendris Benítez, detenida en 2018 y procesada por su presunta vinculación con el supuesto atentado con drones contra Nicolás Maduro; María Auxiliadora Delgado Tabosky, quien permaneció detenida durante más de siete años y fue condenada por terrorismo; y Yolimar Alemán, procesada por su presunta participación en la Operación Gedeón, un presuntp intento de incursión armada contra Venezuela ocurrido en 2020.
En medio de este proceso, organizaciones como el Comité de Familiares de Presos Políticos en Venezuela (Clippve) exigió la liberación “inmediata, plena, incondicional y verificable” de todas las personas que permanecen detenidas por motivos políticos en el país.
La organización sostuvo que algunas de las personas excarceladas todavía están sometidas a presentación periódica, prohibición de salida del país y procesos penales abiertos. Por ello, afirmó que una excarcelación no necesariamente representa el fin de las restricciones o de los procesos que dieron origen a la detención.
“Excarcelación no significa libertad sino perpetuidad de la injusticia fuera de la cárcel”, expresó el comité en el documento.
Ante esta situación, Clippve reclamó la publicación de los nombres de las personas excarceladas, sus boletas de excarcelación y la situación jurídica de cada una, además del acceso de organizaciones independientes a todos los centros de detención para verificar las condiciones de los privados de libertad.

title: Portrait of the Ukrainian Nation at 35 Years of Restored Independence
content:
The first thing I consider extremely important is that Ukraine has overcome the fundamental regional differences we still observed before 2014.
The differences between East and West, South and Center have not disappeared. But they are no longer fundamental. We have become a united country in regional terms.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
For me, this is one of the most positive changes of the independence era. It greatly contributes to social solidarity. And without solidarity, it is impossible to have a viable future in the terrible war we are experiencing today.
In this sense, I would even say that we are now more integrated than many other democratic countries. Look at the US: regional and political divisions largely determine whom society elects and what direction the country takes. In Ukraine, these differences have lost their former sharpness.
There is another extremely important change. Sociology has a methodology for measuring social distance – how close we consider members of different groups to be and how willing we are to accept them, up to the point of being ready to see them as members of our own families.
Before 2014, Ukrainians had the smallest social distance between Russians and Belarusians. Traditionally, they were considered the “closest” to us. After the Euromaidan, the annexation of Crimea, and the beginning of Russian aggression, everything changed.
Today, citizens of Russia and Belarus are among the groups toward whom Ukrainians maintain the greatest social distance. And it is important to stress that we are talking specifically about citizens of these states, not about a person’s ethnic background.
EXPLAINER: 35 Years Ago Today, the World Held Its Breath
At the same time, we have moved significantly closer to Europeans. This is a very important change because there was a paradoxical situation in the past: we declared a European choice, but the average Ukrainian psychologically kept Europeans at a greater distance than Russians.
Now that distance is shrinking.
Ukrainians have always differed significantly from Russians in terms of political culture. We have a different history – not a monarchical-imperial tradition, but experience of living within the European political space, including the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Cossack state.
Ukrainians can be emotional, sometimes even inclined toward ochlocracy, but we are nevertheless democratic.
Our value system is changing as well. For a long time, we were relatively close to Russians in this respect – largely as a result of the Soviet legacy. But in recent years, we have been moving significantly away from it.
I see a shift from security and material well-being as the primary values toward self-realization, freedom, mutual assistance, and tolerance.
What is particularly important is that this shift accelerated after 2022. We have moved closer to the European value system and further away from the system we once shared with Russian society.
We still lack tolerance, of course. War intensifies emotions, and that is natural. But what matters is that Ukraine has vigorous public debates. That is part of a democratic political culture.
At the same time, I do not want to create an overly optimistic portrait.
The war has brought enormous losses. There are practically no people who have not been affected by it. Someone has lost loved ones; someone has lost their home, job, property or place of residence. This inevitably affects the psychological and moral state of society.
Our mood today is worse than it was in the autumn of 2022, when we experienced the highest level of optimism. At that time, around 70-80% of people viewed the future positively. Today, that figure is closer to 60%.
The number of people willing to accept significant concessions to Russia in exchange for ending the war is also growing. I estimate them at roughly 20% of the population.
But that is still a minority. The overwhelming majority of Ukrainians are not prepared to accept the aggressor’s terms. Given all our losses and psychological exhaustion, this is a very important indicator.
It seems to me that we have become more realistic. In 2022, many people were unrealistically optimistic. We thought the war would end within several months or half a year. Now we understand that it is a long process.
But there has been one fundamental psychological change: it is very difficult to live with a sense of being a victim. When Ukraine began systematically destroying Russia’s military potential, Ukrainians saw themselves not only as victims of aggression, but as actors capable of striking back.
We constantly need hope. Not an illusion, but hope – an awareness that we can influence our own future.
I am cautious about forecasts. To be honest, I have become disappointed in the predictive capabilities of sociology around the world.
Why? Because today the world is effectively being run by two old, sick, and deeply insecure politicians, whose decisions, ambitions, whims, resentments, and personal complexes affect the fate of billions of people. We have all become hostages to this situation.
And this is no longer only a problem of war.
The world is undergoing extraordinary changes driven by technological progress, demographic and climate challenges, and economic upheaval. Against this backdrop, people often choose leaders who offer simple solutions to complex problems. They lose their critical thinking and begin to believe in a messiah. Ukrainians, too, believe in their own messiah.
So I would not risk drawing a precise portrait of what a Ukrainian will look like in ten years.
But there is a scientifically grounded method – extrapolation, or projecting patterns of past development into the future. And I know what the trends are.
For us, the main thing is to withstand this war. We will not be abandoned. Otherwise, Europeans will have far more problems than simply helping Ukraine. We need to hold on ourselves and exhaust Russia, as we have been doing over the past six months.
The second important condition is that Europeans must remain consistent in supporting us, and that far-right forces seeking rapprochement with Putin’s Russia must not prevail.
Under these two conditions, I see a prospect for Ukraine’s value-based, normative, and institutional rapprochement with Europe. This means Ukraine will develop a real party system and a genuine system of local government. Then we will achieve our goal: we will become a normal European country. Perhaps a poor one. Perhaps not the most developed. But Eastern European. Not West Asian, but genuinely European.
Over 35 years of independence, we have become a more integrated country. We understand much more clearly how different we are from Russia. We have moved closer to Europe not only politically, but also psychologically and in terms of values.
And despite all the losses, we have preserved what matters most – the majority of Ukrainians remain ready to defend their right to determine their own future.
That is how I approach the 35th anniversary of restored independence: not without anxiety, not without fatigue, but with the understanding that Ukrainian society has become significantly stronger and more mature over these decades than we ourselves are sometimes inclined to believe.

title: Chat-based interaction in virtual classes: EFL students’ perceptions, motivation, and well-being
content: BackgroundDespite the growing body of research concerning online learning technologies in language education, limited attention has been directed toward realizing the affordances of chat-based interaction in a synchronous virtual classroom. This study explores the perceptions of female EFL postgraduate students regarding the use of chat-based interaction in synchronous virtual classrooms, specifically in reference to their motivation and well-being after attending a 15-weeks intensive English course delivered online via Blackboard.MethodsA cross-sectional survey design with a quantitative research methodology was used to collect data from (N = 128) female Saudi postgraduate students enrolled on an online English course for 15 weeks. It drew on correlational methodology to identify any relationships with the student’s demographic information and their perceptions, motivation, and well-being. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability tests, Pearson correlations, a linear regression model, and an independent samples t-test, and Welch’s one-way ANOVA.ResultsThe findings demonstrate a consistent tendency for postgraduate EFL learners to report positive experiences with chat-based interaction in the synchronous virtual classroom. Their perceptions, motivation and well-being were strongly and significantly interrelated, with motivation exhibiting the highest relationship to well-being (r = 0.867, p < 0.001); (B = 0.734, β = 0.704, p < 0.001). The EFL students’ experience using Blackboard virtual classes was associated with a statistically significant difference in their well-being (p = 0.016, p < 0.05); there was no significant difference in any construct by academic major or English-learning experience; age showed a significant omnibus effect on motivation (p = 0.020), attributable to a single pairwise contrast between the youngest and oldest age groups, but no significant effect on perceptions or well-being.ConclusionThe results revealed chat-based interaction is an accommodative, low-anxiety communication method that is associated with engagement and well-being among learners in online EFL settings. It adds to the prevailing literature by promoting knowledge of chat-based interaction as a psychologically and pedagogically significant mode of communication. It further emphasizes the importance of instructors including chat-based activities to create supportive, engaging, and emotionally safe learning environments in virtual classrooms. Given evidence of substantial conceptual and empirical overlap among the three constructs (see Instrument Validity), these findings should be interpreted as exploratory and correlational rather than confirmatory or causal.

title: El Perú que se acerca cuando volar cuesta menos
content:
Todos lo sabemos: el Perú tiene una geografía compleja. Las características de nuestro territorio hacen que trasladarse por tierra entre algunas ciudades -especialmente de la sierra y la selva- pueda tomar muchas horas. En ese contexto, viajar en avión puede significar tiempo ganado, una oportunidad para viajar más y, sobre todo, una forma distinta de conectar al Perú.
La ruta Lima–Cusco ayuda a dimensionarlo. Comprando con anticipación, es posible encontrar pasajes cercanos a S/110, un valor que puede acercarse al de un bus interprovincial, pero con una gran diferencia de tiempo. Más de 16 horas por carretera frente a poco más de una hora por aire.
Esa accesibilidad se ha ampliado en los últimos años. Según la Asociación Internacional de Transporte Aéreo (IATA), entre 2011 y 2023 la tarifa aérea real promedio en el país cayó 54%. Volar sigue teniendo un costo, por supuesto, pero cada vez está más cerca de ser una alternativa al alcance de más peruanos.
Esa es la apuesta de Sky hoy: seguir desarrollando un modelo basado en la eficiencia y la tecnología, que nos permita ofrecer un buen producto a precios accesibles y ampliar la posibilidad de volar a más personas. Lo vimos cuando llegamos a Ayacucho en 2019. Solo en julio de ese año, mes en que iniciamos operaciones hacia ese destino, el tráfico de pasajeros creció cerca de 6% respecto del mismo mes de 2018. El incremento de opciones de vuelo y los precios accesibles contribuyeron a generar nueva demanda. Personas que antes no consideraban el avión empezaron a tenerlo como una opción. Eso es democratizar el acceso: ampliar el mercado, no solo competir por él.
Y cuando eso ocurre, el beneficio no se queda en el aeropuerto. Cuando más personas pueden volar, el impacto se siente también en las regiones. Promperú proyecta cerca de 49,7 millones de viajes por turismo interno en 2026. Cada viaje mueve hospedaje, restaurantes, transporte local, comercio y servicios. Conectar mejor una región significa también acercarla a más visitantes, más consumo y más oportunidades.
La aviación tiene además un impacto económico que pocas veces vemos detrás de un boleto. IATA estima que en el Perú genera 36.100 empleos directos y US$942,8 millones de actividad económica directa. Si sumamos la cadena de valor, el gasto asociado y el turismo, su impacto alcanza los US$6.200 millones y más de 364 mil empleos.
Por eso, hablar de tarifas al alcance de más personas no es hablar únicamente de una estrategia comercial. Es hablar de productividad, descentralización y competitividad. Pero lo avanzado no está garantizado, Perú necesita competencia, infraestructura aeroportuaria que acompañe el crecimiento, regulación eficiente y una estructura de costos que no termine alejando nuevamente al pasajero.
Durante mucho tiempo medimos las distancias del Perú en kilómetros. Tal vez hoy debamos empezar a medirlas también en horas y oportunidades. Si conseguimos que volar siga siendo accesible, no solo tendremos más pasajeros en los aviones, tendremos regiones más cerca, más personas conectadas y un país con mayores posibilidades de crecer.

title: Building more resilient food systems with precision agriculture
content:
Oksana Hrynevych, Agriculture Project Manager at EIT Food, explains why precision agriculture is essential for informing farmers and strengthening our food system
As agriculture faces mounting pressures from climate change, resource scarcity, rising input costs, and increasing demand for sustainable food production, precision agriculture and smart farming are becoming essential tools for the future of farming.
By combining technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), satellite imagery, remote sensing, drones, IoT sensors, and data analytics, farmers can gain deeper insights into their fields and make more accurate, timely decisions. Rather than simply introducing more technology, these approaches empower farmers with actionable information that improves productivity, optimises resource use, and supports long-term environmental sustainability.
EIT Food is Europe’s largest and leading food innovation community, working to connect partners across Europe and fund innovation to build a sustainable, resilient, and healthy food system.
The Innovation Platform spoke to Oksana Hrynevych, Agriculture Project Manager at EIT Food, to explore how precision agriculture can strengthen food system resilience and how EIT Food is helping to drive the adoption of smart farming solutions across the agrifood sector.
What potential do you think precision agriculture/smart farming has to transform farming and food production? How can it strengthen food systems’ resilience?
I think precision agriculture and smart farming have enormous potential, particularly because they allow us to move from farming based mainly on averages and assumptions towards more informed, site-specific, and timely decision-making.
Agriculture is becoming increasingly exposed to uncertainty: climate variability, water scarcity, input costs, soil degradation, and changing market conditions. Technologies such as remote sensing, IoT sensors, satellite data, AI, and decision-support tools can help farmers understand what is actually happening in their fields and respond much more precisely. This can mean applying water, fertilisers, or crop protection products where and when they are really needed, identifying problems earlier, and ultimately producing more with fewer resources.
But I don’t see precision agriculture as a transformation in itself. Its real value comes when technology enables a better farming system. For example, combining field data with agronomic knowledge can support regenerative practices, improve soil and water management, reduce unnecessary inputs and help farmers understand the impact of the decisions they are taking.
From a food-system perspective, this can contribute to resilience by making farms more efficient, adaptive and less dependent on scarce resources, while also generating better data to understand what is happening at farm and landscape level. The opportunity is therefore not simply to make farming more ‘digital’, but to make it more informed, adaptive, and sustainable.
Why is it important for farmers to utilise precision agriculture tools? What challenges can it help overcome?
For me, the main reason is quite simple: farmers are making increasingly complex decisions in an environment where uncertainty is increasing, and they need clear and concise information to make the best one.
A farmer cannot manage every part of a farm in the same way when there can be significant differences in soil, moisture, crop development, or pest pressure even within the same field. Precision agriculture can help reveal those differences and turn data into actionable information.
It can help farmers address challenges such as water scarcity, rising input costs, soil degradation, labour constraints, and climate variability. It can also support earlier detection of problems and more targeted use of inputs, potentially improving both economic and environmental performance.
However, I think we should be careful about assuming that giving farmers more data automatically means better decisions. The challenge is not only collecting data; it is making that data useful, understandable, and actionable. A farmer doesn’t necessarily need another dashboard, but they need a reliable recommendation or insight that helps them decide what to do differently tomorrow.
This is why I strongly believe in combining technology with agronomic expertise, farmer experience, and practical field validation. The best solutions are those that fit into the farmer’s workflow, demonstrate a clear return on investment, and solve a real problem rather than adding another layer of complexity.
Can you share any examples of precision agriculture/smart farming initiatives that EIT is facilitating/supporting?
One example that I find particularly relevant is EIT Food’s Test Farms programme, because it is built around the principle that technologies need to be tested and validated in real agricultural environments, with farmers, rather than remaining at the level of a promising technology or laboratory prototype.
Through Test Farms, EIT Food supports agrifood-tech startups to test and validate their solutions directly on farms. These can include technologies related to remote sensing, farm monitoring, decision-support systems, robotics, soil and crop monitoring, and other digital farming solutions. What is particularly valuable is the connection between startups, farmers, agronomists and other ecosystem actors, because it allows us to understand not only whether a technology works technically, but whether it actually creates value in a real farming context.
More broadly, through EIT Food’s resilient agriculture portfolio, we are also increasingly interested in how digital technologies and data can support the measurement, reporting, and verification of agricultural outcomes. For example, satellite and remote-sensing data can help monitor crop development, land management, and certain regenerative agriculture indicators across much larger areas than would be possible through field measurements alone.
For me, this is where the real opportunity lies: using smart farming technologies not as an isolated digital layer, but as an enabler of the transition towards more resilient and regenerative agricultural systems.
A recent example, in terms of startups that we work with, is Atfield Technologies, whose precision viticulture platform was tested through the Test Farms programme in vineyards in Spain. By combining sensor data, weather intelligence and predictive analytics, the solution helped growers improve decision-making around disease management, irrigation, and harvest planning while reducing resource use.
Alongside farmers, who else does EIT Food support to implement and understand precision agriculture?
I think one of EIT Food’s strengths is precisely that it does not look at innovation from the farmer’s perspective alone. Agricultural transformation requires an ecosystem.
We work with startups and technology providers, helping them validate their solutions in real agricultural environments and understand the needs of farmers. We also work with corporates and food companies, which increasingly need better data and tools to understand and transform their agricultural supply chains.
Agronomists and advisors are also extremely important. They are often the bridge between technology and the farmer, translating data into practical recommendations and helping farmers integrate new solutions into their existing management systems.
Beyond that, there is a role for research organisations, universities, investors, policymakers and other ecosystem actors. Each brings a different piece of the puzzle: from developing the technology and generating evidence, to financing adoption, creating the right policy environment and scaling successful solutions.
And I think this is particularly important for precision agriculture because adoption is not only a technology challenge; it is an ecosystem and behaviour-change challenge. A solution can be technically excellent, but if it doesn’t fit the farmer’s reality, if the business case isn’t clear, or if there is no support to interpret the information, it is unlikely to scale.
This thinking is also reflected in EIT Food’s Landscape Model, which works across entire agricultural landscapes rather than focusing on individual farms in isolation. The model brings together farmers, food companies, technology providers, advisors, researchers, investors and public authorities to align incentives, generate evidence and support the adoption of tools, including precision agriculture solutions, that can help deliver measurable environmental and economic outcomes at scale.
I see EIT Food’s role as helping to connect these different actors so that innovation moves from the technology provider, through validation and knowledge, all the way to practical adoption on farms and, ultimately, impact across the food system.

title: On the fence about a statin? In borderline cases, calcium scans could be a tiebreaker
content:
When it comes to predicting heart attacks and strokes, what matters the most: a number, a picture, or both?
It depends on the patient, two new trials say, adding to previous research exploring the value of coronary artery calcium (CAC) scans when combined with risk measured by the newly adopted PREVENT calculator. Both tools assess the future chances of serious cardiovascular events, potentially influencing decisions about prescribing cholesterol-lowering statins or other treatments to limit damage to blood vessels leading to the heart and brain.
In borderline cases, calcium could be a tiebreaker. But for most people, there’s no need for the tests, despite their growing popularity as personalized measures of wellness.
PREVENT risk estimates rely on standard information gathered in a doctor’s visit, while CAC scans, not typically covered by insurance, can cost the patient $100 to $400. But there’s another way to see calcium buildup, hiding in plain sight (almost). CT scans done for other reasons performed just as well as CAC-specific scans when predicting coronary heart disease, cardiovascular disease, and deaths over the next 10 years, research published in Circulation in July concluded.
Whatever the reason for the CT scan, the images can reveal calcium deposits stiffening the arteries, worsening plaques made by excess fats and “bad” LDL cholesterol. (The improvement when doing both tests may be modest, on the order of 1% or 2% in people referred for cardiovascular disease screening.)
The PREVENT equations are designed to flash warning signals about plaque formation. As the foundation for guidelines issued earlier this year by the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association, their goal is to identify precursors of serious cardiovascular events by relying on blood pressure, cholesterol, age, family history, and current illnesses such as inflammatory disease, diabetes, kidney disease, cancer, HIV, and certain reproductive conditions.
PREVENT classifies risk over the next 10 years as low (under 3%), borderline (3% to 5%), intermediate (5% to 10%), and high (10% or higher). CAC scores range from 0 to 1,000 or higher, with risk climbing from none at 0, to mild under 100, moderate up to 300, and severe over 300.
Neither PREVENT nor CAC gives a hard-and-fast rule for when to recommend statins, the well-established and affordable medications that can significantly lower cholesterol and disease risk. That’s something doctors and patients should discuss, in conversations that should begin as early as age 30, the guidelines now say.
The ACC-AHA guidelines do recommend using incidental calcium findings to inform decisions on statins for men age 40 and up and women age 45 and up who are living with borderline or intermediate 10-year risk of heart attack or stroke. The 2018 guidelines had suggested them only for people at intermediate risk.
The question prompting the recent research is how.
The two studies appearing in August both examined data following just over 6,000 people age 45 to 79 for 10 years in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis. They analyzed whether CAC scores made a difference in predicting who would later have a heart attack or stroke. The answer is yes, but only when PREVENT risk is classified as borderline or intermediate.
“Adding CAC to PREVENT for everybody only modestly improves statistical prediction,” Michael Shapiro, co-author of the study published Aug. 18 in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology, told STAT via email. He is a preventive cardiologist at Wake Forest University School of Medicine whose research and practice focus on lipids, atherosclerosis, and prevention of cardiovascular disease.
“The main message is that not everyone needs a CAC scan and CAC zero should not be used as a veto against statin therapy,” he said. “CAC was most helpful as a tiebreaker when a patient was at borderline risk and the statin decision was unclear.”
The JAMA study published Wednesday also found that overall, CAC did not change the predictions made by PREVENT. But in a secondary analysis of people considered at intermediate or borderline risk by PREVENT, a different answer emerged, co-author Nilay Shah, a preventive cardiologist at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine who studies risk prediction for cardiovascular disease, said.
“You get a much more substantial, quote, ‘reclassification,’ meaning people who were in the borderline and intermediate risk category, when they got a calcium score,” Shah told STAT in an interview. “We much better identified those who had a heart disease event later, within the next 10 years, and we much better identified those who didn’t have a heart disease event in the next 10 years.”
In the JACC study, some patients who qualified for statin treatment because their PREVENT risk was 5% or higher had more heart attacks, strokes, or other events, even though their CAC reading was zero.
“CAC may still help explain risk, improve adherence, and guide how intensive prevention should be, but generally should not be used to avoid treatment,” Shapiro said. “Our findings support a guideline-centered role for CAC in the PREVENT era. Mainly, refining risk near the treatment thresholds, helping put absolute risk into context, and informing the intensity of preventive efforts.”
What should patients and their doctors do?
If people already have a calcium score, it should be incorporated into their risk assessment, Harlan Krumholz, a cardiologist and health outcomes researcher at Yale University, told STAT. He was not involved in the studies. Others may want the test, even when it is unlikely to change a decision about starting a statin, because knowing whether coronary atherosclerosis is actually present has value to them and may influence how they think about prevention.
“I would distinguish the value of ordering the test from the value of knowing the result,” Krumholz said. “These studies help us be more disciplined about when to order CAC solely to resolve a treatment decision.”
Patient interest in CAC scans may be growing, perhaps inspired by artificial intelligence-based algorithms that automate opportunistic screening, which got a nod in March in the ACC-AHA guidelines. Shah wonders if something else is at play with CAC images.
“We can estimate somebody’s risk with a calculator, and you get a number,” Shah said. “Or you can actually see an image of your heart and say, OK, that’s actually what’s going on in my heart. I think that appeals to a lot of people because it’s much more tangible.”

title: Zero-Shot Adaptation of Medical Vision Foundation Models for High-Frequency Micro-Ultrasound Prostate Segmentation
content: Prostate cancer claims a life every 80 seconds. Early detection is needed to prevent disease progression, and both PSA density calculation and biopsy decisions rely on knowing the exact boundary of the gland. Conventional ultrasound at 6-12 MHz blurs this boundary, missing one in three high-risk cancers. Micro-ultrasound (29 MHz) improves resolution threefold but introduces dense acoustic speckle that obscures the outer wall; given the same image, two clinicians draw outlines differing by over 10% in area. Supervised methods are costly and generalise poorly across scanners. Can a foundation model segment the prostate with no training data? We present the first zero-shot pipeline for this modality: MedSAM, pre-trained on over 1.5 million medical images, localises the prostate; we then apply CLAHE to sharpen the outer wall, binary dilation to recover missed pixels, and Fourier smoothing (4 modes, s=1.05) to refine the boundary. MedSAM requires a spatial prompt, so we evaluate bounding-box and point-click strategies across 75 patients of the Micro-Ultrasound Prostate Segmentation dataset (2,621 slices). On the 20-patient held-out test set, the pipeline reduces mean boundary-distance error by 45% (Dice 0.749+/-0.043 to 0.865+/-0.029; HD95 217.2+/-36.9 to 120.1+/-26.1 px), reaching Dice 0.859 across the cohort. Its mean overlap shows no significant difference from the three non-expert rater groups (p>0.19), while segmenting 38-52% more consistently (lower inter-patient standard deviation). Point-click prompts fail regardless of placement (best Dice=0.350), because speckle gives no stable local contrast. Only an approximate bounding box is required, so any clinic can deploy it without data collection, annotation, or retraining.

title: Foro Penal confirmó la excarcelación de 72 presos políticos hasta la mañana de este sábado
content:
El vicepresidente de Foro Penal, Gonzalo Himiob, confirmó este sábado que al menos 72 presos políticos fueron excarcelados en Venezuela, en un proceso que arrancó el viernes tras el cierre de la primera ronda de negociaciones entre representantes de la oposición y el gobierno.
"A las 10 a. m. Hasta esta hora desde Foro Penal podemos confirmar la excarcelación el día de ayer de 72 presos políticos. 55 hombres y 17 mujeres. Seguimos trabajando en el proceso de verificación", precisó Himiob a través de su cuenta de la red social X.
Según reportaron en redes sociales las ONG que monitorean la situación de los detenidos por razones políticas en el país, las primeras liberaciones ocurrieron en los centros penitenciarios de Yare II, Rodeo I y el Instituto Nacional de Orientación Femenina (INOF).
La organización Realidad Helicoide confirmó, por su parte, la salida de Daniel Zambrano Arias, Yolimar Alemán, Marifrancys Marcado y Emirlendris Benítez. A esto se sumó la difusión de un video que registró la salida de un grupo de otros 25 ex presos políticos de El Rodeo I, entre ellos Elías Noriega, Javier Morillo, Merwin Simons y Jesús García.
El propio Foro Penal había adelantado el viernes, hasta las 5:00 de la tarde, la confirmación de al menos 40 personas liberadas por motivos políticos, una cifra que se fue actualizando conforme avanzaba el proceso de excarcelación en distintos centros de detención del país.
El listado de excarcelados de El Rodeo I incluye también a Naudy Laya, Julio Elías Jiménez, Leomard Bravo, César Burgos, José Trejo, Yorman Solórzano, Edward Pérez, José Félix Carrizales, Williams Lizardo, José Ignacio Moreno, Audelino Bermúdez, Miguel Medina, Randolf Rivas, Jesús Rojas, Yohanny López, Ramir Pocaterra, Raimer López, Arturo Sairias, Daesger Hernández, Christian Quintero y Leomar Guerra.
Excarcelaciones en Venezuela
El mensaje de Himiob se produce luego del comunicado emitido por Miguel Pérez Pirela, ministro de Comunicación e Información, a través del cual destacaron que serían en total 131 personas las que recibirían ‘medidas alternativas a la privación de libertad’.
"Las referidas medidas fueron acordadas por los tribunales de la República, a petición del Ministerio Público, luego de que este Programa solicitara a los órganos del Sistema de Justicia Penal evaluar la situación jurídica de personas procesadas o condenadas por delitos relacionados con diversos atentados contra la institucionalidad democrática, la paz y el desarrollo de la República", reza parte del comunicado del gobierno.
"El Programa para la Paz y la Convivencia Democrática ratifica que continuará decididamente apoyando las iniciativas del Gobierno Nacional y de la sociedad civil organizada orientadas a favorecer el reencuentro entre los venezolanos, el fortalecimiento del tejido social de la nación y la consolidación de la paz de la República", cierra el texto.
En tanto, Dinorah Figuera, presidenta de la Asamblea Nacional electa en 2015, celebró la excarcelación de los presos políticos en diversos centros penitenciarios del país.
"Con esperanza por el reencuentro de las familias venezolanas recibimos la información de las excarcelaciones. No son todos y merecen libertad plena, sigamos exigiendo sin descanso hasta que cada ciudadano se reencuentre con su familia", indicó Figuera.

title: Equipos de Conalep de Guanajuato triunfan en Roborave de Japón
content:
El plantel Silao logró el primer lugar en la categoría Sumo 3 kg
Domingo 23 de agosto de 2026, p. 6
La Secretaría de Educación Pública (SEP) informó que estudiantes del Colegio Nacional de Educación Profesional Técnica (Conalep) plantel Silao, ubicado en Guanajuato, obtuvieron el primer lugar del Roborave International World Championship 2026, realizado en Osaka, Japón.
El equipo Mantarraya, integrado por Saúl Azael Valdenegro Vázquez, Juan Tadeo Rea Elías, Juan Diego Rodríguez Ramírez y Christian Yahir Sandoval Rivas, obtuvo el primer lugar mundial en la categoría Sumo 3 kg, con un robot autónomo construido y programado por los propios estudiantes.
El prototipo, equipado con diversos sensores, identifica superficies y líneas para definir su ruta y localizar a su oponente dentro del “dojo”, con el objetivo de embestirlo y sacarlo de la superficie.
Al respecto, el titular de la SEP, Mario Delgado Carrillo, señaló que este resultado, ademas de ser un motivo de orgullo para México, “refleja el talento, la creatividad y la formación técnica de los estudiantes del Conalep, quienes mediante el conocimiento y la innovación, demuestran que desde las aulas públicas del país es posible competir y alcanzar los más altos niveles internacionales".
Resultado de un trabajo en equipo
El director general del Conalep, Rodrigo Rojas Navarrete, señaló que estos resultados son producto de un modelo que combina trabajo en equipo, disciplina, creatividad y conocimiento, mediante el cual se forman profesionales técnicos altamente calificados y jóvenes capaces de transformar sus comunidades.
Informó que en la competencia, que reunió a 304 equipos provenientes de 12 países, también destacaron estudiantes del Conalep Valle de Santiago, en Guanajuato, el cual obtuvo el cuarto lugar en la categoría Sumo 3 kg, mientras que el equipo Gowan, del mismo plantel, logró el quinto sitio en Sumo 1 kg.
Asimismo, mencionó que estudiantes del plantel Río Bravo, Tamaulipas, que fue la única delegación mexicana y latinoamericana en la categoría Soccer Bot, consiguieron el segundo lugar mundial en el rango High School, con un equipo integrado por Martha Infante, Denilson Espinoza, Ángel David Montero y Ximena Lumbreras, asesorados por el coach Santos Vargas.

title: Free to publish, free to read: Qatar's open science bet
content:
Researchers publishing on QScience.com pay nothing to appear and readers pay nothing to download — a model the Qatar-based platform says has made it the first fully open-access publishing house of its kind in the Middle East, now drawing more than 400,000 users a year.
The platform hosts over 10,000 published works, of which about 3,450 articles, books and chapters carry authors affiliated with Qatari institutions, Dr Salah B Ajjur, head of academic and journals publishing at QScience.com, told Gulf Times in an exclusive interview.
"QScience.com is a peer-reviewed, open-access scholarly publishing platform from Qatar," Dr Ajjur said, adding that most of the content sits in the platform's catalogue alongside books, book chapters and conference proceedings.
The 3,450 figure covers items where Qatar appears in the affiliation metadata — typically research linked to Qatar-based institutions — which he described as a useful public indicator of Qatar-connected output on the platform.
QScience.com is part of Hamad Bin Khalifa University Press under Qatar Foundation, providing a digital home for scholarly journals, books, conference proceedings and special collections, and connecting researchers in Qatar and the wider Arab world with a global readership.
Operating as a diamond open-access imprint, the platform makes research freely available to read, download and reuse worldwide under a Creative Commons Attribution licence, with authors retaining copyright. Dr Ajjur said it is the first 100% open-access publishing house of its kind in the Middle East, with more than 15 years of publishing behind it.
He said the platform combines rigorous peer review with a transparent, author-centred process, and runs a bilingual English-Arabic interface to support both regional and international scholarship.
For Qatar-based researchers, he said, the result is a locally rooted but internationally visible outlet — one that carries work from Qatar Foundation institutions, universities, hospitals, ministries and scholarly societies to audiences worldwide without the paywalls that can restrict access to scholarly research. Professional publishing services include peer review, subject-expert copyediting, digital preservation, and marketing and discoverability support.
QScience.com has partnerships with major institutions in Qatar and across the Middle East, and its bilingual environment supports scholarship in both Arabic and English. This ensures research generated in Qatar is not only produced but properly published, preserved, discovered and used, locally and internationally, in service of national development goals, Dr Ajjur said.
Journals on the platform charge no article processing fees and content is accessible without subscriptions — a model he said lowers the barrier to publishing openly, and one aligned with Qatar National Vision 2030 and other national priorities, encouraging research that contributes to national development goals while meeting international scholarly standards.
By publishing work focused on Qatar-specific and regional priorities while holding to international standards, he said, the platform helps local researchers contribute both to Qatar's knowledge economy and to the wider global scholarly community. Since its launch it has strengthened the country's research ecosystem by providing a durable and internationally credible outlet for scholarship produced in and about Qatar and the Middle East.
Dr Ajjur said QScience.com collaborates internationally through publishing partnerships, industry memberships, indexing relationships and shared technical infrastructure, ensuring research published in Qatar meets global standards and is discoverable worldwide.
"Together, these collaborations and indexing activities embed QScience.com within the international scholarly communications ecosystem while keeping a strong focus on regional research impact and Qatar's national priorities," he added.

title: Moncorvo, el pueblo portugués que rinde homenaje a Borges en plazas, monumentos y hasta en la avenida principal
content:
Moncorvo, el pueblo portugués que rinde homenaje a Borges en plazas, monumentos y hasta en la avenida principal
En el Día del Lector y a 127 años del nacimiento del escritor, los lazos borgeanos con Portugal reaparecen en la historia de su bisabuelo paterno, Francisco, que emigró desde Moncorvo, donde Borges es ciudadano ilustre
- 9 minutos de lectura'
Los lazos entre Portugal y Jorge Luis Borges, del que este lunes se conmemora el 127° aniversario de nacimiento, no son pocos. Por empezar, uno de los antepasados del escritor, su bisabuelo paterno Francisco Borges, partió a mediados del siglo XIX desde Torre de Moncorvo, localidad portuguesa del distrito de Braganza, para embarcarse en una expedición militar rumbo al Río de la Plata. “Nada o muy poco sé de mis mayores / portugueses, los Borges…”, refiere el autor en un poema de El hacedor. Borges viajó cuatro veces a Portugal.
En su biografía Jorge Luis Borges. Un destino ejemplar, el investigador Lucas Adur consigna que, en 1817, el joven teniente lusitano Francisco Borges, nacido en Torre de Moncorvo, desembarcó en la Banda Oriental en una expedición militar, a las órdenes del brigadier Lecor. “Finalizada la invasión y firmada la paz en 1828, Borges decidió permanecer en la República Oriental del Uruguay, y en 1829 contrajo matrimonio con Carmen Lafinur, hija de un antiguo militar navarro, Luis Lafinur y de una dama cordobesa, María Viviana Pinedo Montenegro”, indica. El abuelo paterno de Borges fue el coronel Francisco Isidoro Borges Lafinur, nacido en Montevideo, Uruguay, y fallecido en combate en la Batalla de La Verde.
Francisco Borges pertenecía a una familia descendiente de “nuevos cristianos” portugueses: los tatarabuelos de Borges fueron Manuel António Cardoso [Borges] (en el siglo XX, algunos miembros de la familia se sumaron a la llamada “Obra de Redención”, un movimiento de reintegración al judaísmo rabínico) y María Antonia [¿Ramalho? Borges?], natural de Mogadouro, ambos de Torre de Moncorvo. En 1984, el bisnieto escritor, Premio Cervantes 1979, sería declarado ciudadano honorario de Moncorvo.
El único escritor portugués mencionado por Borges en ensayos y conferencias, y al que dedica un poema, es Luís de Camõens, autor del poema épico Os Lusíadas (1572), “tu Eneida lusitana”, según le dice Borges, donde se narran los viajes del navegante Vasco da Gama. También escribió una detallada entrada sobre la literatura portuguesa para la Enciclopedia Jackson, de 1952. Entre las veintiocho conferencias inéditas reunidas por Sara Luisa del Carril para el flamante Conferencias reunidas 1960-1985, hay dos dedicadas a Camõens (ambas de 1972, a cuatrocientos años de la publicación de Os Lusíadas).
En 1924, al final de su segundo viaje a Europa, Borges pasó parte del mes de mayo en Lisboa. Como dijo en su madurez, le hubiera gustado conocer a Fernando Pessoa, de quien entonces no sabía nada. El ensayista uruguayo Emir Rodríguez Monegal imaginó que Borges y Pessoa se cruzaron, jóvenes, en las calles de Lisboa. En Autobiographical Essay, Borges resalta de su paso por Europa en aquellos años “many memories of Geneva, Zurich, Nimes, Córdoba, and Lisbon”.
Cuando Borges y María Kodama viajaron a Portugal, en 1984, el escritor fue declarado ciudadano honorario de Torre de Moncorvo. Sin embargo, nunca llegó a visitar el pueblo de su bisabuelo paterno (ubicado a unos 400 km de Lisboa).
Desde 2008, en Lisboa, frente a la embajada de Portugal en la Argentina se halla el Jardín Jorge Luis Borges, con un memorial dedicado al escritor porteño y donde está grabado en piedra el poema “Los Borges”, aquella “vaga gente que prosigue en mi carne, oscuramente, sus hábitos, rigores y temores”, como dicen los versos. La obra escultórica es del argentino Federico Brook.
En 2021, en Torre de Moncorvo se inauguró el Monumento a los Escritores, con una estatua de Borges y de los portugueses José Saramago y Miguel Torga, obra del escultor Hélder de Carvalho. Pero el primer tributo moncorvense a Borges data de 1997, cuando la avenida principal de la localidad fue bautizada con su nombre. En esa ocasión, el presidente de Portugal, Jorge Sampaio, viajó hasta el pueblo medieval para asistir a los homenajes al escritor argentino de raíces portuguesas.
En una entrevista concedida a la Radio Televisión Portuguesa en 1984, Borges habló de Torre de Moncorvo: “Siento nostalgia por un lugar que no conozco; imaginaba Torre de Moncorvo con montañas, pinos, casas blancas con tejados de tejas, un lugar pequeño y tranquilo, quizás olvidado y con una agradable melancolía típica de Portugal”. Y rindió tributo a escritores portugueses, como Eça de Queiroz y su amado Camõens. Entrevistada en 1999 por el diario portugués Público, Kodama contó que Borges dormía con un ejemplar de la obra de Camõens en su cabecera.
En diálogo con LA NACION, el arqueólogo e historiador portugués Rui Leonardo, que integra la División de Cultura, Turismo y Artes de la Municipalidad de Torre de Moncorvo, señala que varios escritores portugueses fueron referentes para Borges; además de Camõens y Queiroz (“a quien conoció a través de su madre”, observa), Borges le escribió una carta a Pessoa para el volumen Fernando Pessoa, poete pluriel, publicado en Francia en 1985: “La sangre de Borges de Moncorvo y Acevedo (el Azevedo) me ayuda a comprenderte sin geografía, Pessoa. No te costó nada renunciar a las escuelas y a sus dogmas, a las vanidosas figuras de la retórica y a la opinable tarea de representar a un país, una clase o una época. Sin duda, jamás te preocupó tu lugar en la historia de la literatura. Tengo la certeza de que estos homenajes sonoros te sorprenden, te sorprenden pero te emocionan. Hoy eres el poeta del Portugal. Inevitablemente, alguien pronunciará el nombre de Camõens. No faltarán las fechas caras a toda celebración. Tú escribías, sin embargo, para ti, no para la gloria. Juntos, vamos a compartir tus versos; déjame ser tu amigo”.
“En 1960, Borges ya había escrito un artículo con Alicia Jurado sobre la literatura portuguesa del siglo XX -agrega Leonardo-. En ese artículo cita a Alberto Caeiro, seudónimo de Pessoa a quien define así: ‘Se le comparó con Walt Whitman, mereció el epíteto de genio y su influencia se hizo sentir a ambos lados del Atlántico’”. En Torre de Moncorvo, la obra de Borges está disponible en la Biblioteca Municipal y en la Biblioteca Escolar.
El historiador portugués afirma que Borges comenzó a investigar sus orígenes portugueses en la década de 1970, con la ayuda de su cuñado, Guillermo de Torre, y su sobrino, Luis Guillermo de Torre. “Incluso contactó al escritor Luís Lobo de Oliveira, quien le envió el certificado de matrimonio del bisabuelo con María del Carmen Lafinur, en Montevideo, que indica que Francisco Borges era natural de Torre de Moncorvo, Reino de Portugal -destaca-. Posteriormente, en la década de 1980, el origen moncorvo de los antepasados de Borges fue confirmado por el padre Joaquim Manuel Rebelo y António Júlio Andrade, el sobrino de Borges, y también por Lux-Wurm, quien tiene un artículo que crea el árbol genealógico en el número 22 de la Revista del Instituto Argentino de Ciencias Genealógicas, de 1987″.
“En Portugal, la figura de Borges es ampliamente reconocida -concluye-. Aquí, en Torre de Moncorvo, lo consideramos hijo de la tierra. Ya le hemos rendido homenaje con la avenida que lleva su nombre, inaugurada en 1997 en presencia del presidente de la República, Jorge Sampaio. Además, está el Monumento a los Escritores, inaugurado en 2023. También apoyamos el documental de Erika Grinberg sobre los orígenes portugueses de Borges, que se estrenará próximamente”.
En Nuestro Borges, los documentalistas Erika Grinberg y el estadounidense Charlie Siskel (uno de los directores de En busca de Vivian Maier) adaptaron al formato audiovisual la historia de la búsqueda de los archivos sobre los antepasados portugueses de Borges. “Es un trabajo que lleva ya muchos años de trabajo y, felizmente, estamos viendo ya la conclusión -dice Grinberg a LA NACION-. El documental aborda, por un lado, la investigación genealógica que hicieron en el pueblito medieval, muy especial, de Torre de Moncorvo, de donde surgió el dato de que de ahí habría salido el bisabuelo paterno de Borges. En ese entonces, yo vivía en Portugal y estuve a cargo del registro que hacían las autoridades de Moncorvo. Por otro lado, empecé con entrevistas a los vecinos del pueblo, a la gente del lugar. Todos querían contar algo sobre una eventual posible relación que ellos tenían con Borges. Eran todas historias muy divertidas y, por supuesto, inverosímiles”.
“En Moncorvo, Borges es una figura totalmente omnipresente -resume Grinberg-. La avenida principal del pueblo se llama Jorge Luis Borges, hay monumentos a Borges, frases de Borges en los edificios oficiales. Y todo este mundo de mitos y leyendas que se empezó a generar alrededor de él, cuya obra en realidad pocos habían leído, sirvió para convertir un trabajo institucional en una película de otras características. Conseguimos que María Kodama formara parte del proyecto. Cuando le conté todo lo que me había encontrado en Moncorvo, María me dijo: ‘Erika, me estás contando un cuento de Borges’. La idea es representar eso también: este mundo borgeano que se generó alrededor del mismo Borges”.
Durante la investigación sobre los antepasados del escritor se reveló que Torre de Moncorvo formaba parte de la Ruta de las Juderías. “Cuando echan a los judíos de España, muchos se instalan en esta zona -dice-. Una de las versiones es que los Borges eran una familia marrana y que en realidad no se llamaban Borges, tenían otro nombre”.
El proyecto audiovisual cuenta con el apoyo de la Fundación Internacional Jorge Luis Borges, la Fundación Saramago, el Instituto Camõens, la embajada de Portugal en la Argentina, la embajada de la Argentina en Portugal y la Organización de Estados Iberoamericanos. Mientras tanto, borgeanos de todo el mundo esperan el estreno de Nuestro Borges.

title: Syyrian presidentti nimitti neuvonantajakseen lakkautettujen SDF-joukkojen ex-komentajan
content:
Syyrian presidentti Ahmed al-Sharaa on nimittänyt neuvonantajakseen kurdijohtoisten SDF-joukkojen entisen komentajan Mazloum Abdin. Asiasta kertoi Syyrian valtiollinen uutistoimisto Sana perjantain vastaisena yönä.
Abdi ilmoitti tiistaina SDF-joukkojen lakkauttamisesta itsenäisenä toimijana. Joukot liitettiin osaksi Syyrian asevoimia.
Lakkauttaminen oli osa alkuvuodesta tehtyä sopimusta liittää joukot ja kurdien siviilihallinto Syyrian keskushallinnon alaisuuteen.
Neuvottelut SDF-joukkojen liittämisestä asevoimiin alkoivat viime vuoden alkupuolella sen jälkeen, kun Syyrian itsevaltaisen johtajan Bashar al-Assadin hallinto oli kaatunut joulukuussa 2024. Prosessi junnasi kuitenkin pitkään paikoillaan, ja tilanne kärjistyi tämän vuoden tammikuussa viikkojen mittaisiksi taisteluiksi Pohjois- ja Koillis-Syyriassa.
Vuonna 2015 Yhdysvaltain tuella perustetut SDF-joukot olivat merkittävässä roolissa äärijärjestö Isisin torjumisessa.
SDF-joukkojen liittäminen osaksi Syyrian hallintoa oli merkittävä voitto koko Syyrian hallinnon yhtenäisyyttä ajavalle al-Sharaalle, mutta samalla se päätti ainakin toistaiseksi Syyrian kurdien itsehallintohaaveet.
Tammikuun taisteluiden aikana al-Sharaa allekirjoitti määräyksen, jossa sitouduttiin turvaamaan kurdien kulttuurillisia ja kielellisiä oikeuksia. Määräyksessä taattiin myös kurdeille Syyrian kansalaisuus sekä oikeus kurdinkieliseen koulutukseen.

title: Lenkijos „PGE Dystrybucja“ brigados pradėjo elektros atkūrimo darbus Marijampolės regione
content:
Po audros daliai Lietuvos gyventojų penktadienį dar neatkūrus elektros tiekimo, Marijampolės regione darbus pradėjo Lenkijos elektros skirstymo operatoriaus „PGE Dystrybucja“ brigados su specialia technika, penktadienį pranešė „Energijos skirstymo operatorius“ (ESO).
Vienas didžiausių Lenkijos skirstomųjų tinklų operatorių „PGE Dystrybucja“ į pagalbą ESO atsiuntė dvi brigadas, kurias sudaro 11 specialistų, į Lietuvą jie atsigabeno dvi keltuvo platformas – „Mercedes 4x4“ ir „Iveco 4x4“.
Brigados padės tvarkytis su audros padariniais pietų Lietuvoje.
„Šios audros mastas yra toks, kad kiekviena papildoma profesionalų brigada šiandien yra itin svarbi. Mūsų kaimynai ne tik gerai supranta, ką reiškia tokio masto stichija – jie patys susiduria su panašiais iššūkiais ir žino, kokio sudėtingumo darbai laukia. Todėl ypač vertiname Lenkijos kolegų sprendimą atvykti ir padėti mums būtent tada, kai pagalbos labiausiai reikia“, – pranešime sako ESO vadovas Renaldas Radvila.
Pasak jo, vienas didžiausių iššūkių šalinant tokio masto stichijos padarinius yra žmogiškųjų išteklių pajėgumai.
Anksčiau šią savaitę į pagalbą ESO atėjo Lietuvos perdavimo tinklų operatorė „Litgrid“, pašalinusi audros padarinius savo tinkle.
Kaip skelbiama, bendrovė sustabdė planinius darbus, kuriuos galima atidėti, ir visoms rangovų bendrovėms, kurios specializuojasi oro linijų darbuose, pasiūlė padėti ESO tvarkyti skirstomąjį tinklą.
Kaip skelbė ELTA, po smarkios audros šalyje daliai gyventojų ir verslų vis dar neturint elektros, o ūkininkams skaičiuojant nuostolius, Vyriausybė šį trečiadienį paskelbė ekstremaliąją situaciją valstybės mastu.
Penktadienio rytą elektros tiekimas vis dar buvo sutrikęs 46 tūkst. ESO klientų.

title: De la sequía al milagro: cien años de fe en El Consejo, por Rafael A. Sanabria M.
content:
De la sequía al milagro: cien años de fe en El Consejo, por Rafael A. Sanabria M.
Correo: [email protected]
Existen instituciones cuya permanencia no obedece al mero azar cronológico ni a la inercia de fríos decretos formales, sino a la pulsión sagrada, casi telúrica, del espíritu humano. En la geografía íntima de Aragua, la Sociedad de Nuestra Señora del Carmen de Pequeños Agricultores se erige no solo como un santuario devocional, sino como un monumento vivo a la persistencia.
Este jueves 20 de agosto de 2026, al consumarse un siglo exacto de su gestación institutiva, la mirada histórica rebasa la sola evocación piadosa para desentrañar un prodigio sociológico: la victoria del esfuerzo colectivo sobre la inclemencia del tiempo y del olvido.
La génesis de esta epopeya menor germinó en las entrañas de la adversidad. En los albores de 1926, con el estigma reciente de la devastadora sequía de 1925 erosionando los campos y amenazando con esterilizar las siembras de El Martillo, La Arvenca y las vegas ribereñas de Tiquire Flores, la comunidad de conuqueros de El Consejo transformó la angustia en plegaria ecuménica.
Bajo la copa protectora de un tamarindo centenario, en el patio arbolado del comisario Valentín Mosqueda en la otrora calle de Barrialito (hoy calle Urdaneta), aquellos hombres de faz curtida redactaron las primeras actas sobre una austera mesa de madera. Aquella convergencia de voluntades halló pronta respuesta en el firmamento; de esa alianza indisoluble entre el trabajo telúrico, la fe y la providencia brotó la entidad popularmente consagrada como la «Sociedad de los Conuqueros».
En la textura oral del pueblo, el advenimiento del mes de agosto articulaba un decir categórico: «¡Ya vienen las fiestas de los patones!». Lejos de entrañar un matiz peyorativo, la locución era una afirmación estética y de alta dignidad social.
Denominar «patones» a los labradores constituía la metonimia popular para definir la impronta del campesino: aquellos pies ensanchados por el contacto directo con el surco, descalzos o ceñidos a la humilde alpargata, que arrastraban el barro fecundo de la tierra trabajada. La huella ancha del «patón» era el holograma vivo de la productividad, la rúbrica indeleble con que el agricultor modelaba el sustento de la comarca.
Aquella directiva fundacional –vertebrada por Felipe Suárez en la presidencia, Félix Tovar Padrón, Trino González, Valentín Mosqueda, Pulido Padrón, Juan Díaz, Florencio López y Juan Tovar, respaldada por un nutrido cabildo de labradores– echó los cimientos institucionales. No obstante, el mayor mérito reside en la cadena ininterrumpida de custodios que le sucedió.
A lo largo de cien años, la veneración a la Virgen del Carmen no declinó gracias a la entrega metódica de generaciones que rehuyeron la grandilocuencia para cultivar la gratitud. Nombres de densidad histórica como Rafael Mellado, Elías Manzano, Alejandro Natera, Carlos Barrios Padilla, en conjunción con el temple matricial de mujeres de la talla de Raimunda Díaz y Ana Teresa de Delgado –la insustituible «Negra Aguilera»–, inscribieron sus afanes en las páginas amarilleadas de los libros de actas, convirtiendo la festividad –con sus altares callejeros y la ofrenda pública de cambures, topochos, naranjas y tomates en los bailes de las calles Sucre, Campo Elías o la avenida Bolívar– en una lección magistral de solidaridad comunitaria.
Allí radica, precisamente, la verdadera enseñanza magistral que esta sociedad religiosa lega a toda la nación venezolana. En un país cuya historia suele medirse por las grandes gestas heroicas o los caudillismos efímeros, este grupo de modestos labradores demuestra que la verdadera cohesión social se edifica en lo cotidiano, mediante una fe encarnada en la fraternidad real.
*Lea también: Resistir en la costa, por Nelson Oyarzábal P.
La gran lección para la colectividad es que las crisis verdaderas –aquel suelo árido y agrietado que a menudo amenaza con paralizar el destino de la patria– no se superan desde la resignación pasiva ni desde la dispersión individualista, sino mediante la organización humilde, la constancia colectiva y la certidumbre espiritual. Esta institución nos enseña que el dogma sin obras es terreno yermo, y que la trascendencia de un pueblo se mide por su capacidad de sostener, contra viento y marea, el compromiso sagrado con sus tradiciones y con el prójimo.
Contemplada a un siglo de distancia, la peripecia histórica de estos conuqueros trasciende el mero marco localista para transformarse en una lección republicana de urgencia contemporánea. La Sociedad de los Pequeños Agricultores reclama hoy su sitial como un baluarte incontrovertible de la reserva moral de Venezuela.
En una época caracterizada por la fugacidad y el desencanto, la gesta de este abnegado grupo de hombres y mujeres nos recuerda que la fe genuina trabaja en el tiempo presente para la eternidad. Es esa convicción inamovible la que hoy sostiene esta tradición centenaria: un faro ético que conmina a la nación entera a reencontrarse con la nobleza de sus raíces y a labrar, con el temple indeclinable de aquellos pioneros, el porvenir fecundo de la tierra que nos cobija.
Rafael Antonio Sanabria Martínez es profesor. Cronista de El Consejo (Aragua).

title: Peaceful protest is fundamental right, but authorities must act if it turns violent: HC
content:
Peaceful protest is fundamental right, but authorities must act if it turns violent: HC
The Punjab and Haryana High Court said citizens have a fundamental right to peaceful protest but authorities must intervene when demonstrations turn violent or threaten public safety.
The Punjab and Haryana High Court Friday underlined that while citizens have a fundamental right to peaceful protest, authorities are duty-bound to step in when such a protest turns violent or threatens public safety.
A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor was hearing the PIL filed by Chandigarh resident and advocate Vivek Singla, seeking directions to the Chandigarh Administration, police and the states of Punjab and Haryana to maintain law and order in Chandigarh and restrain protesters from organising or entering the city in large numbers on August 15 or any other date in the wake of the protest call by Quami Insaf Morcha.
The court observed, “It is well settled that, in a democracy, citizens have a fundamental right to assemble and express their views through peaceful protest. Such a right ought not to be interfered with by the authorities. However, where a protest ceases to be peaceful, turns violent, or poses a threat to public safety, the competent authorities are duty-bound to take appropriate preventive and remedial measures in accordance with law to ensure the maintenance of public peace, order, and security.”
The Bench said, “We hope and trust that Punjab and Haryana, as well as Chandigarh, shall act with due sensitivity and responsibility and ensure that no untoward incident is permitted to occur. We expect that all necessary preventive and remedial measures, as warranted in law, shall be taken for the protection of the life, liberty, and security of the public at large in accordance with law.”
The Bench has listed the matter for August 20, by when the respective status reports in this regard are to be filed by Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.
The PIL was taken up out of turn on special mentioning by the petitioner, who is a practising advocate of the High Court.
At the outset, on the oral request of senior counsel representing the petitioner, the court directed that the Haryana Home Secretary be impleaded as respondent in the PIL and directed the Registry to amend the memo of parties accordingly.
Story continues below this ad
Through his counsel senior advocate RS Khosla, Singla submitted that such protests often lead to grave law-and-order situations in which the public at large is made to suffer for no fault on its part.
The petition stated that Quami Insaf Morcha had given a nationwide call to gherao the Punjab Governor seeking release of Bandi Singhs and that news reports had mentioned that various religious leaders would also join the call and participate in the morcha. It further stated that the morcha had announced that a large number of people would arrive in Chandigarh on August 15 to surround the Governor’s House.
Through Khosla, the petitioner submitted that the right to assemble could not supersede the wider public’s right to safety, life and free passage on public thoroughfares. The petition sought directions to protest organisers, unions and groups to refrain from holding demonstrations without prior administrative clearance and to abstain from violence, vandalism or forcible road blockades.
The petitioner also sought directions to the Chandigarh Administration and police, as well as Punjab, to maintain open transit and emergency corridors, disperse unsanctioned blockades and hold violent or non-compliant organisers strictly accountable under law.
